        2. Scan the list from the right and remember the first index *r* (from
           the right) at which the element also appears earlier in the list.
        3. If *l* ≤ *r* the result is the slice x[:r]; otherwise the result is
           the slice x[l+1:].

    """
    n = len(x)

    first_repeat_left = None
    seen = set()

            # the first occurrence is earlier, therefore the element at the
            # earlier position is the one that repeats later.
            # we keep the index of that earlier position.
            first_repeat_left = next(j for j in range(i) if x[j] == v)

    last_repeat_right = None

            # this is the *second* occurrence from the right; the later
            # occurrence is at a higher index, so the element at the higher
            # index repeats earlier.
            last_repeat_right = next(j for j in range(i + 1, n) if x[j] == v)
            break
        seen.add(v)

    if first_repeat_left is None and last_repeat_right is None:
        # no repetitions at all – keep the whole list
        return x[:]

        # only a right‑side repetition exists
        return x[:last_repeat_right]
    if last_repeat_right is None:
        # only a left‑side repetition exists
        return x[first_repeat_left + 1:]

    # both sides have repetitions – keep the longer resulting slice
    left_slice = x[:last_repeat_right]
    right_slice = x[first_repeat_left + 1:]

    such that **no element of the remaining part occurs both
